    LYON is a Mexican team formed in October 2024 following a partnership between ⁠⁠Movistar R7 and ⁠⁠Six Karma. The brand used to be one of the most successful clubs in Latin America. For its history, see Lyon Gaming.

    History[]

    The Golden Era: Lyon Gaming (2013 - 2017)[]

    Lyon Gaming was founded in April 2013 by Karzek, FraGio, and Nikez with the sole purpose of creating a highly competitive team to represent the Latin American region.[1] From their inception, they were considered the team to beat due to the individual mechanical talent of their players.

    During 2014 and 2015, the team began to solidify its absolute dominance in regional tournaments, but it was in 2016 and 2017 when the squad reached legendary status under the leadership of franchise players such as Édgar "Seiya" Bracamontes, Sebastián "Oddie" Niño, Matías "WhiteLotus" Musso, Daniel "Jirall" del Castillo, and Diego "Arce" Chang.

    In 2016, Lyon qualified for their first official international Riot Games event, the IWCI 2016, although they fell short of expectations. However, they returned stronger for the IWCQ 2016, where they had a historic performance and narrowly missed qualifying for the World Championship (Worlds), falling in an agonizing 5-game series against Russia's Albus NoX Luna.

    2017 was a perfect year regionally: they won both the Opening and Closing tournaments undefeated in the Liga Latinoamérica Norte (LLN). This earned them tickets to the MSI 2017 and the Worlds 2017, where they showcased a great level in the Play-In stage, facing teams from major regions like Cloud9 and Team WE.

    Despite their monumental success (securing 11 regional championships in LAN), a controversy arose in late 2017: the organization discovered it did not legally own the rights to the "Lyon Gaming" name and logo. Former player Marcelo "Thyak" Ramones retained the trademark rights. After failed negotiation attempts, the team was forced to leave the lion name behind and reinvent itself for the 2018 season.

    The Rainbow Reign: Rainbow7 and Movistar R7 (2018 - 2024)[]

    Reborn as Rainbow7 (R7) on December 5, 2017, the organization continued to rule with an iron fist. Despite an initial suspension of WhiteLotus that hindered their preparation for the LLN Opening 2018 and an early playoff elimination during the Closing season, the organization prepared for a new challenge: the unification of LAN and LAS into the new Liga Latinoamérica (LLA) in 2019.[2]

    In their first LLA season (2019), the team restructured with former players from rival teams like Dash9. However, it was in 2020 when R7 returned to international glory. With a roster featuring talents like Josedeodo, Aloned, and Leza, the team achieved a historic final in the LLA Closing 2020: they pulled off a "reverse sweep" (coming back from 0-2 to win 3-2) against All Knights. This secured their spot at Worlds 2020, where they set a milestone by securing a historic victory against China's (LPL) fourth seed, LGD Gaming, during the Play-In stage.

    Between 2021 and 2022, the team (now named Movistar R7 for sponsorship reasons) maintained competitive rosters by bringing in great international talents and veterans, but their second "golden era" arrived in 2023. R7 became the third team in history to achieve a back-to-back championship in the LLA by winning both the Opening and Closing splits in 2023, qualifying for MSI 2023 and Worlds 2023. By 2024, they continued to dominate the league, cementing themselves as the most decorated institution in Latin American history with 16 regional championships.

    The Return of the Lion: LYON in the Americas (2024 - Present)[]

    In mid-2024, Riot Games announced a massive restructuring of the competitive ecosystem in the Americas, eliminating the LLA and creating the pan-American league LTA (League of Legends Championship of The Americas), divided into North and South conferences. [3]

    On October 31, 2024, following a partnership agreement between the management of Movistar R7 and Six Karma, the organization was accepted as a Partner Team in the LTA North. Seizing this turning point, the management managed to revive and recover the original name and identity: the lion was back, now simply under the name LYON.

    Their return brought them back to the spotlight. For the 2025 season, they brought back veteran Peruvian jungler Oddie and signed North American talent Licorice, but the team had bittersweet results in the early LTA North splits.

    It wasn't until the roster reshuffle ahead of 2026 that LYON made the North American region tremble. Under the guidance of head coach Reignover, LYON built a superteam by incorporating top laner Dhokla, star Polish jungler Inspired, talented Korean AD Carry Berserker, Korean mid laner Saint, and Oceanic support Isles. This historic roster swept the preseason and was crowned champion of the LCS 2026 Lock-In after defeating Cloud9 3-1, giving the franchise its first official trophy competing in North America, and the 17th regional championship in the organization's history.

    Trivia[]

    • They are the second most decorated team at a domestic level with 18 regional titles, winning 16 of them as Latin American champions and 2 as North American champions.
